body:
`case_study:ricoh-india-2016` | 2016-07-19 | tickers: RICOHINDIA | confidence: verified

Ricoh India (Japanese parent held ~74%) admitted in Jul 2016 that its accounts were falsified; the estimated FY16 loss was Rs 1,123 cr (later Rs 1,118 cr) versus a company with a market cap of only a few thousand crore. A PwC forensic audit found unsupported out-of-books entries of Rs 66.7 cr in Q1FY16 alone that turned a Rs 64 cr loss into a Rs 2.7 cr profit; reports suggest the fraud began in FY14. SEBI barred 7 key managerial personnel in Feb 2018 and ordered a fuller forensic audit; the shares were suspended and the parent later recapitalised via NCLT, leaving minority holders with little. Visible flags: (1) the stock ran from ~Rs 100 to above Rs 1,000 in 2013-15 on a sudden revenue surge (services/'managed document' contracts) -- revenue growth far ahead of the parent and peers; (2) trade receivables and unbilled revenue rose faster than sales; (3) Q2FY16 results were delayed and the statutory auditor (BSR/KPMG) raised concerns; (4) thin free float (~26%) helped the run. Lesson: 'MNC parent' is not a governance guarantee for the Indian subsidiary; receivables growing faster than revenue plus delayed results is a classic pre-blowup combination (Beneish DSRI/TATA flags).

**Lesson:** MNC tag is not a shield; check DSO trend
**Spotted early by:** statutory auditor (refused to sign Q2FY16)
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:forensic-redflag-checklist`, illustrates -> `insight:auditor-exit-signal`
**Sources:** <https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/ricoh-india-admits-accounting-violations-falsification-of-books-116071901198_1.html> ; <https://business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/sebi-orders-forensic-audit-of-ricoh-india-s-books-over-fraud-case-118021300003_1.html> ; <https://www.bloombergquint.com/markets/did-the-fraud-at-ricoh-india-begin-much-before-the-company-claims>

body:
`insight:india-cycle-top-bottom-signals` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: india, base-rate, process, redflag

Tops (each appeared before or at the 1992, 1994, 2000, 2008, 2018, 2021 and 2024 peaks): (1) issuance boom with falling issuer quality - 1993-96 small IPOs, Reliance Power (Jan 2008), 2021 loss-making tech IPOs, 2024 SME IPOs subscribed hundreds of times; (2) leverage or unusual funding - bank receipts (1992), badla and co-op bank money (2000), project/land loans (2007), NBFC lending (2017-18), retail F&O (2021-24); (3) narrative stocks valued on non-cash metrics - land banks, order books, GMV, 'nation-building'; (4) valuation extremes - Sensex P/E 27-35x, Nifty >24x, market cap/GDP >120-150%, smallcap/midcap P/E above large caps; (5) breadth divergence - small caps peak first (Jan 2018, Sept/Dec 2024) while the index makes new highs; (6) regulator warnings/tightening (SEBI on SME IPOs 2024, MF stress tests 2024). Bottoms (2001-03, Oct 2008-Mar 2009, Aug 2013, Mar 2020, early 2025/2026 for small caps): P/E ~11-15x, mcap/GDP <70%, IPO drought, FPI capitulation (record outflows, ownership at multi-year lows - 15.8% in 2026), rupee panic followed by a forceful RBI/government response, and defensives leading. No signal times the turn; combinations of 3+ have marked zones where adding risk (bottoms) or trimming it (tops) paid off over 2-5 years.

| key | value |
|---|---|
| top_signals | issuance quality, leverage, narrative valuation, P/E/mcap-GDP extremes, breadth divergence, regulator action |
| bottom_signals | P/E 11-15x, mcap/GDP<70%, IPO drought, FPI capitulation, currency panic + policy response |

body:
- **Measures** it can check against screener: revenue YoY / QoQ / absolute (quarter, half or FY),
  EBITDA margin (screener OPM, which excludes other income, or including other income when the
  promise says so), PAT growth / absolute, finance cost % of revenue, debtor days, ROCE, FCF,
  dividend payout and borrowings. Capex counts only if it is in a CSV or `--derived-capex` is set,
  because screener has no capex line and the balance-sheet proxy is rough.
- The scorer **does not touch** segment, export, order-book/inflow, capacity, market-share,
  "normalised"/ex-FX or company-defined working-capital metrics (pilot lesson 7). These keep the
  LLM or human status.
- **Thresholds** are fixed across companies (pilot lesson 4):
  - Growth targets: delivered within max(0.5 pp, 5% of the target); partly within max(2 pp, 20%).
  - Margin, ROCE and finance-cost targets: delivered within 0.3 pp; partly within 1.5 pp.
  - Amounts and days: delivered at 95% of the target or better; partly at 80-95%.
  - Explicit floors and ceilings ("25% plus", "below 4.5%") are strict: delivered only if met;
    partly if within 2.5% (relative).
  - Beating a target counts as delivered.
  - A level target met on the TTM figure one quarter after the deadline counts as partly.
- **Fuzzy deadlines.** The period scored is the fiscal period that contains the deadline. Per-quarter
  run-rate targets are divided by the number of quarters in that period. Vague or missing deadlines
  default to the fiscal year two years after the call and are flagged.
- **Supersedes chains.** Promises are grouped by the LLM's `chain_key`, or by `measure+period`.
  Without either, they are clustered by category and metric-token Jaccard similarity; per-period flows
  only chain within one fiscal year, and ordinal words ("second 75k block") must match.
  - A later statement with the same target is linked with `restates`.
  - A later statement with a lower target or a later date is linked with `supersedes`. If it was not
    flagged `acknowledges_revision`, that is a **goalpost move**, counted once per new statement.
  - Final status: an earlier promise that was quietly superseded and whose original target was not
    met becomes `moved-goalpost`. If the revision was acknowledged, it becomes `withdrawn`.
- **"Silently dropped?"** is only ever a *suggestion*: a material, unresolved promise that is not
  restated in the following 4 calls (pilot lesson 5).
